newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stad Rotterdam sees extra eps growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Stad Rotterdam sees extra eps growth in 1997.

text.p: Medium-sized insurer Stad Rotterdam said on Tuesday earnings per share growth would outpace the group's net profit growth in 1997.

Stad Rotterdam said earlier that it would issue 1.4 million new shares to finance part of the takeover of the remaining 45 percent in 55-percent owned unlisted insurer Amersfoortse, but that it would also pay some of the takeover price in cash.
"Say 1997 profits grew by 10 percent, which is only a figure for the sake of argument, earnings per share would rise by 11.8 percent," chairman Carlo de Swart told a news conference.
Stad Rotterdam said in April it was in talks to buy the remaining 45 percent in Amersfoortse and that it envisaged listing the merged company.
The listing of the new company, ASR Verzekeringsgroep NV, was expected to take place in June.
The insurer said earlier today it would pay about 400 million guilders for the remaining 45 percent in Amersfoortse.
"Stad Rotterdam had bought the 55 percent stake in Amersfoortse in 1983 for 27.5 million guilders," De Swart said.
Stad Rotterdam said today it would pay 190 million guilders in cash to Nuernberger Beteiligungs AG, which had a 20 percent stake in Amersfoortse.
Muenchener Rueck, which had a 25 percent stake in Amersfoortse, will hold an interest of about 12 percent in the combination of Stad Rotterdam and Amersfoortse.
Stad Rotterdam said it was paying 107.5 million guilders in new shares to Muenchener Rueck and 130 million guilders worth in existing shares.
De Swart would not specify the amount of cash the company would have left after it had paid for the deal with Amersfoortse.
Stad Rotterdam has said it does not rule out further acquisitions in its home base.
"If we do another acquisition it would not be a deal worth billions" De Swart said. "We have to remain realistic."
He added that it could again opt for financing an acquisition in cash and in shares.
In April Stad Rotterdam said that its 1996 net profit grew by 17.6 percent to 156.9 million guilders and that it targets an average growth of profits of at least eight percent per year.
Stad Rotterdam aims to increase its market share in life and non-life business, which were both seen at about 5.2 percent in 1996, up from an average market share of about 4.4 percent in 1990.
